description: The image displays two pie charts, labeled (a) and (b), each illustrating the proportional distribution of specific linguistic or lexical categories. Chart (a) breaks down the frequency of common English function words: “the” (31%, blue with diagonal stripes), “this” (21%, light blue with horizontal lines), “for” (17%, green with crosshatch pattern), “to” (15%, yellow with dots), “in” (9%, light blue with vertical lines), and an unlabeled gray segment (7%, solid gray). Chart (b) presents a different set of categories: “the” (38%, blue with diagonal stripes), “$” (27%, pink with crosshatch), “equilibrium” (19%, yellow with dots), and “consonant” (15%, gray with dots). Both charts include a legend above each pie, matching colors and patterns to category labels, and display percentage values directly on each slice. The segments in both charts are ordered approximately by descending size, with the largest segment positioned at the top-right. The visual design uses distinct textures and colors to differentiate categories, with no exploded slices or additional annotations beyond the percentages and labels.
